analysis.title: GS Chart of the Day: Beta Chase (Guillaume Soria, 2 Oct 2026)
key_insights: High-beta equities have been weighed down over the past few months by rising oil prices, higher yields and geopolitical uncertainty, leaving the beta factor emerging from one of its most volatile stretches in recent history.
Beta is among the most rate-sensitive factors in the market, and GS has seen continued demand for beta hedging in recent months in anticipation of a higher-rate regime.
Today's softer payroll print pushed yields lower without being weak enough to raise recession fears. GS says this could be a strong tailwind for equities.
Weak market breadth and light net positioning leave room for a catch-up rally from laggards.
For upside on high-beta stocks, GS likes its sector/industry-neutral basket GSPUBETA.
For clients managing beta exposure, GS likes hedging with its Beta-ex-AI pair GSPUBETX. Beta exposure in the Prime book is at the 83rd percentile over the last 5 years.
High-beta themes are linked to the AI complex and remain high momentum: AI Semis (beta 1.40, YTD 91%), Memory (1.22, YTD 191%) and AI Inference Chips (0.85, YTD 114%).
Low-beta and negative-beta themes include Oil (-1.64), Bond Proxies (-1.22), Nat Gas (-1.12), Geopolitical Risk (-1.08) and Expensive Defensives (-1.08).
The correlation of the GS beta pair to momentum has been strongly positive in the last few years.
GSPUBETX has underperformed the Beta basket while maintaining consistently high correlation, which GS presents as the reason it works as a hedge.
The GS Beta Pair has been trending with AAII Investor Sentiment bullish readings.
